items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to calculate the following limit:

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \pi/2}\dfrac{\sin{2x}}{2\cos{x}}]

Content:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit by directly substituting [MATH: x=\dfrac{\pi}{2},] we get an indeterminate form:

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → π/2)(\sin 2x)/(2\cos x)|= (\sin (2 ⋅ (π)/(2)))/(2\cos ((π)/(2))); = (\sin (π))/(2\cos ((π)/(2))); = (0)/(0)]

Content:
However, if we simplify the fraction before attempting to evaluate the limit, we obtain a more clear result.

Content:
To simplify the fraction in this particular case, the double angle formula for sine will be useful:
[MATH: \sin{2x}=2\sin{x}\cos{x}]

Content:
Using the double angle formula above, we have

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → π/2)(\sin 2x)/(2\cos x)|= lim_(x → π/2)(2\sin x\cos x)/(2\cos x); = lim_(x → π/2)(2\sin x\cos x)/(2\cos x); = lim_(x → π/2)\sin x; = \sin ((π)/(2)); = 1.]

Content:
In other cases, we may need to use a different trigonometric identity.

sections.normalized_html: [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \pi/4}\dfrac{\sin^2{x}-\cos^2{x}}{2\sin{x}\cos{2x}}=]
sections.readable_text: [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \pi/4}\dfrac{\sin^2{x}-\cos^2{x}}{2\sin{x}\cos{2x}}=]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit directly, we get an indeterminate form:

[MATH: lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x\cos 2x)|= (\sin^{2} ((π)/(4)) − \cos^{2} ((π)/(4)))/(2\sin ((π)/(4))\cos (2 ⋅ (π)/(4))); = (1 − 1)/(sqrt(2)\cos ((π)/(2))); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. The double angle formula for cosine will be useful in this case: [MATH: \cos{2x}=\cos^2{x}-\sin^2{x}]

Using the double angle formula above, we have [MATH: lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x\cos 2x)|= lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x(\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x)); = lim_(x → π/4)(− (\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x))/(2\sin x(\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x)); = lim_(x → π/4)(− (1)/(2\sin x)); = − (1)/(sqrt(2)); = − (sqrt(2))/(2).]

sections.normalized_html: Evaluate [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to 0}\dfrac{1-\cos x}{3\sin^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}.]
sections.readable_text: Evaluate [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to 0}\dfrac{1-\cos x}{3\sin^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit directly, we get an indeterminate form:

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(1 − \cos x)/(3\sin^{2} ((x)/(2)))|= (1 − \cos (0))/(3\sin^{2} (0)); = (1 − 1)/(3 ⋅ 0); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. Again we will use the double angle formula for cosine, but in a different form:

[MATH: \cos{x}=1-2\sin^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)]

Substituting the above formula, we get

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(1 − \cos x)/(3\sin^{2} ((x)/(2)))|= lim_(x → 0)(1 − (1 − 2\sin^{2} ((x)/(2))))/(3\sin^{2} ((x)/(2))); = lim_(x → 0)(2\sin^{2} ((x)/(2)))/(3\sin^{2} ((x)/(2))); = lim_(x → 0)(2)/(3); = (2)/(3).]

sections.normalized_html: [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to (-\pi/2)}\dfrac{\cos^2x}{1+\sin x}=]
sections.readable_text: [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to (-\pi/2)}\dfrac{\cos^2x}{1+\sin x}=]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit directly, we get an indeterminate form:

[MATH: lim_(x → (− π/2))(\cos^{2} x)/(1 + \sin x)|= (\cos^{2} (− (π)/(2)))/((1 + \sin (− (π)/(2)))); = (0)/(1 − 1); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. In particular, we will use the Pythagorean identity:

[MATH: \cos^2{x}=1-\sin^2{x}]

Substituting the above formula, we get

[MATH: lim_(x → (− π/2))(\cos^{2} x)/(1 + \sin x)|= lim_(x → (− π/2))(\cos^{2} x)/(1 + \sin x); = lim_(x → (− π/2))(1 − \sin^{2} x)/(1 + \sin x); = lim_(x → (− π/2))((1 + \sin x)(1 − \sin x))/(1 + \sin x); = lim_(x → (− π/2))(1 − \sin x); = 1 − \sin (− (π)/(2)); = 1 − (− 1); = 2.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit directly, we get an indeterminate form:

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7\tan^{2} x)|= (\sec (0) − 1)/(7\tan^{2} (0)); = (1 − 1)/(7 ⋅ 0); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. In particular, we will use the Pythagorean identity for tangent and secant:

[MATH: \tan^2{x}=\sec^2{x}-1]

Substituting the above formula, we get

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7\tan^{2} x)|= lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7(\sec^{2} x − 1)); = lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7(\sec x − 1)(\sec x + 1)); = lim_(x → 0)(1)/(7(\sec x + 1)); = (1)/(7(\sec (0) + 1)); = (1)/(7(1 + 1)); = (1)/(14).]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that we want to calculate the following limit:

Content:
[MATH: \lim_\limits{x\to \pi/2}\dfrac{\sin{2x}}{2\cos{x}}]

Content:
If we attempt to evaluate this limit by directly substituting [MATH: x=\dfrac{\pi}{2},] we get an indeterminate form:

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → π/2)(\sin 2x)/(2\cos x)|= (\sin (2 ⋅ (π)/(2)))/(2\cos ((π)/(2))); = (\sin (π))/(2\cos ((π)/(2))); = (0)/(0)]

Content:
However, if we simplify the fraction before attempting to evaluate the limit, we obtain a more clear result.

Content:
To simplify the fraction in this particular case, the double angle formula for sine will be useful:
[MATH: \sin{2x}=2\sin{x}\cos{x}]

Content:
Using the double angle formula above, we have

Content:
[MATH: lim_(x → π/2)(\sin 2x)/(2\cos x)|= lim_(x → π/2)(2\sin x\cos x)/(2\cos x); = lim_(x → π/2)(2\sin x\cos x)/(2\cos x); = lim_(x → π/2)\sin x; = \sin ((π)/(2)); = 1.]

Content:
In other cases, we may need to use a different trigonometric identity.

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating a Limit Using a Double Angle Formula

[MATH: lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x\cos 2x)|= (\sin^{2} ((π)/(4)) − \cos^{2} ((π)/(4)))/(2\sin ((π)/(4))\cos (2 ⋅ (π)/(4))); = (1 − 1)/(sqrt(2)\cos ((π)/(2))); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. The double angle formula for cosine will be useful in this case:
[MATH: \cos{2x}=\cos^2{x}-\sin^2{x}]

Using the double angle formula above, we have
[MATH: lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x\cos 2x)|= lim_(x → π/4)(\sin^{2} x − \cos^{2} x)/(2\sin x(\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x)); = lim_(x → π/4)(− (\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x))/(2\sin x(\cos^{2} x − \sin^{2} x)); = lim_(x → π/4)(− (1)/(2\sin x)); = − (1)/(sqrt(2)); = − (sqrt(2))/(2).]

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7\tan^{2} x)|= (\sec (0) − 1)/(7\tan^{2} (0)); = (1 − 1)/(7 ⋅ 0); = (0)/(0)]

So we need to simplify the expression. In particular, we will use the Pythagorean identity for tangent and secant:

[MATH: \tan^2{x}=\sec^2{x}-1]

Substituting the above formula, we get

[MATH: lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7\tan^{2} x)|= lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7(\sec^{2} x − 1)); = lim_(x → 0)(\sec x − 1)/(7(\sec x − 1)(\sec x + 1)); = lim_(x → 0)(1)/(7(\sec x + 1)); = (1)/(7(\sec (0) + 1)); = (1)/(7(1 + 1)); = (1)/(14).]
